name: OpenAI ChatGPT Projects
description: OpenAI's consumer ChatGPT Projects — digital workspaces ('folders') that group related conversations, uploaded reference files, and per-project custom instructions, with optional project-scoped persistent memory. Distinct from Codex Cloud; this is the consumer chat product with project-scoped history.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Account required. Users sign in to ChatGPT with an OpenAI account via email+password or OAuth (Continue with Google / Microsoft / Apple). No anonymous Projects usage. Business/Enterprise/Edu workspaces are org-managed with SSO/SAML and workspace-level admin controls. Identity is account- and (for org plans) workspace-scoped. As of Sept 3, 2025 Projects is available to Free users worldwide.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Collaboration added for org plans. As of Sept 25, 2025, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users can share a Project and invite teammates to collaborate in the same project (shared files, instructions, and context). Consumer Free/Plus/Pro Projects are personal (single-user). Org workspaces provide tenancy isolation; project-only memory can be enabled at the workspace level for Enterprise/Business when Memory is enabled. For Business/Enterprise/Edu, project content is not used to train models by default.

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A 'Project' is an account-scoped (or workspace-scoped for org plans), fully virtual folder-like entity in OpenAI's cloud — not a directory or repo. It bundles grouped chats, uploaded reference files, and per-project custom instructions into one persistent working context. It does not map to a filesystem path or git repo; it is a named container for conversations + files + instructions stored server-side.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Conversations are scoped to a Project. A chat created inside (or moved into) a Project inherits that project's custom instructions and file context. Users can run multiple separate conversations within the same Project, and chats outside projects exist at the account level. With project-only memory enabled, chats can reference other conversations within the same project but not conversations outside it.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Workspace-level (per-project): uploaded files and custom instructions apply to every chat in the project. Project memory can be configured as project-only (self-contained — references only same-project chats) keeping it isolated for sensitive work. Session-level: each chat's running token context (memory does NOT expand the per-response context window). Global/account-level: ChatGPT's general cross-chat memory (saved memories + reference chat history) when not using project-only mode. Custom instructions hold several thousand characters per project.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: No on-disk config files — this is a cloud chat product. Behavior is shaped by per-project Custom Instructions (set in project settings) layered with the project's files and project/global memory settings. Effective precedence: per-project custom instructions + project files (workspace-level) on top of account-global custom instructions and saved memories; project-only memory mode further restricts cross-project context. No AGENTS.md-style file cascade. [uncertain]
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Each Project has a bounded file set acting as its source corpus, uploaded via the UI. Per-project file caps scale by plan: Free up to 5, Plus/Go/Education 25, Pro/Business/Enterprise 40 files per project (max 10 files per batch upload). File size/processing caps include ~512MB per file, ~2M tokens for text/docs, ~50MB for CSV/spreadsheets, 20MB images; Plus/Free get text extraction only while Enterprise supports visual retrieval from PDFs. ChatGPT references project files automatically across the project's chats.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Cloud-managed storage in OpenAI's backend (specific engine not publicly documented). Project memory is implemented as system-generated 'memory logs' — snippets the model extracts from project chats that it judges important — plus the saved files and custom instructions, all persisted server-side and mutable. Org workspaces honor a configured data residency region. Exact databases/cache/event format are undisclosed. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.session_history: Conversations are stored server-side, grouped under their Project, and browsable in the ChatGPT UI. Chats persist until manually deleted. Account/workspace data export is available (consumer export via settings; org exports via admin) producing a downloadable archive. Project messages inherit the workspace's configured retention duration and residency region. Exact export format and per-message schema are not publicly documented. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Two clear layers plus ephemeral state: (1) user-authored durable layer = per-project custom instructions and uploaded files; (2) auto-generated memory = system-created 'memory logs'/snippets extracted from project chats (rolled out Aug 22, 2025 as project-only memory), analogous to automatic sticky notes the system decides matter; and (3) ephemeral per-chat token context = short-term. Project-only memory keeps the auto-memory self-contained to the project (no cross-contamination), separate from ChatGPT's global saved-memories store.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: Within a project, ChatGPT can reference and pull context from prior chats and files in the same project automatically (project memory). Project-only memory limits this to same-project conversations. ChatGPT also has account-wide chat-history reference ('Reference chat history' / 'Reference saved memories') when project-only mode is not used. This lets new chats build on prior context without manual copy-paste. Full-text vs. semantic search specifics for the project history are not publicly detailed. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Chats and projects persist until manually deleted. Deleted projects (and their chats, files, and custom instructions) are removed from OpenAI's systems within 30 days unless legal/security exceptions apply. Files attached to a Project are retained until the Project is deleted, then purged within ~30 days. Org workspaces apply their configured retention duration and residency region to project messages. Archiving vs. hard-delete: deletion schedules permanent removal within 30 days.

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: No user-facing VM/container/worktree — ChatGPT Projects is a managed cloud chat context, not a code-execution sandbox. Isolation is logical: per-project partitioning of files/instructions/memory, project-only memory mode for self-containment, and org/workspace tenancy isolation for Business/Enterprise/Edu (with residency region). Code interpreter / tool execution runs in OpenAI's managed runtime, not a user-controlled sandbox. This product is explicitly distinct from Codex Cloud's executing environments. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: Not applicable in the filesystem/environment sense. There is no saveable machine/env state — only conversation history, uploaded files, custom instructions, and memory logs persist. No separate filesystem/package snapshot independent of conversation content.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Cloud-only consumer product (web, desktop, mobile apps), hosted by OpenAI. No self-hosting and no cloud-to-local execution handoff for Projects. (Codex CLI/Cloud is a separate product line.)
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: Single-conversation interaction model; a user can hold multiple independent chats within a project but there is no managed parallel-agent/worktree fanout or coordinator orchestration in the consumer Projects product. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Sessions are initiated through the ChatGPT web app, desktop app, and mobile apps. Projects are not triggered via Slack/GitHub/cron in this consumer product. Same account/workspace login across surfaces; org plans add admin/SSO entry control.

implementation.implementation_stack: Proprietary, hosted by OpenAI; internal stack not publicly documented. Known characteristics: OpenAI account auth (email/password + Google/Microsoft/Apple OAuth; SSO/SAML for org workspaces); cloud-managed storage of grouped chats, project files, and per-project custom instructions; auto-generated 'memory logs' extracted from project chats for persistent project memory; project-only memory mode for isolation; plan-tiered file caps (5/25/40) and rolling upload limits (e.g., ~80 files/3h on Plus); 30-day deletion window; configurable org retention duration and data residency region. Exact databases, caching, retrieval mechanism, and event format are undisclosed. [uncertain]
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Strong mapping. ChatGPT Projects validates a project_id as an abstract, account/workspace-scoped folder key — analogous to a Labmate workspace_id stored as a MongoDB document holding per-project instructions + file references, with conversations linked by project_id. The 'project-only memory' toggle is a direct precedent for a scoping flag controlling whether a session may retrieve cross-thread context within the workspace only vs. globally — implementable as a query filter on LangGraph thread_id / Mongo session docs keyed by workspace_id. The auto-generated 'memory logs' pattern (system-extracted important snippets, separate from raw files) maps to a derived long-term memory collection in MongoDB distinct from the verbatim session transcript, while ephemeral chat context maps to Redis Streams active-session state with TTL. The 30-day deletion window and workspace-configured retention/residency suggest implementing per-workspace TTL and region tags. Org-shared projects (invite teammates) map to multi-user workspace membership keyed off the connector identity (e.g., Discord), with single-user personal projects as the default tier.
